claims.statement: Leonardo recorded an observation in Rimini dated 8 August 1502.
claims.confidence_basis: Urbino University Press binds the dated observation to Manuscript L folio 78r; independent evidence review is still pending.

claims.statement: Leonardo was present in Cesena by 10 August 1502 in the selected survey context.
claims.confidence_basis: Urbino University Press binds the 10 August Cesena entry to Manuscript L folio 46v; independent evidence review is still pending.

claims.statement: The selected Cesena survey context is associated with Manuscript L folios 9r through 10r.
claims.confidence_basis: The institutional itinerary names folios 9r, 9v and 10r, but the frozen source set has no critical-edition locator or rights-compliant facsimile that independently verifies this separate wall-survey association. It is rejected from the Gate C supported Claim set without asserting that the association is historically false.

claims.statement: Cesare Borgia's letter patent for Leonardo is dated 18 August 1502.
claims.confidence_basis: The university chronology reproduces the full patent text and dating formula at printed p. 16 n. 26; independent evidence review is still pending.

claims.statement: Leonardo recorded the Cesenatico port context on 6 September 1502.
claims.confidence_basis: Urbino University Press binds the dated Cesenatico entry to Manuscript L folio 66v; independent evidence review is still pending.

claims.statement: The selected dated Cesenatico port entry is associated with Manuscript L folio 66v.
claims.confidence_basis: The university chronology transcribes the dated entry and identifies folio 66v; folio 68r is not used as evidence for the exact date.

claims.statement: Royal Collection item 912284 associates Leonardo's Imola map with his autumn 1502 work context.
claims.confidence_basis: Specific collection item candidate; the exact supporting catalogue passage still requires review.

claims.statement: Royal Collection item 912686 catalogues Leonardo's sketches of the street plan of Imola.
claims.confidence_basis: The collection identity is stable, but the source object has not been reviewed for historical geometry use.

claims.statement: The selected sources describe Leonardo as serving Cesare Borgia in an engineering capacity during 1502.
claims.confidence_basis: The published patent transcription supports the commissioned title; the exact end of the State and original-document custody locator remain unresolved.

claims.statement: The Metropolitan Museum of Art chronology dates the rule of Isma'il I to 1501 through 1524.
claims.confidence_basis: Specific institutional chronology entry; content review has not yet occurred.

claims.statement: The institutional source records identify Leonardo da Vinci as the creator or subject of the selected manuscript and map records.
claims.confidence_basis: Museo Galileo and Royal Collection Trust institutional records identify Leonardo; independent evidence review is pending.

claims.statement: The published patent transcription identifies Cesare Borgia as the issuing authority and Leonardo as Architect and Engineer General.
claims.confidence_basis: The university-press transcription at printed p. 16 note 26 supplies the selected identity and title context; review is pending.

claims.statement: The dated 8 August 1502 manuscript entry names Rimini as its observation context.
claims.confidence_basis: The university chronology supplies the place name and folio locator; no point geometry is asserted.

claims.statement: The dated 10 August 1502 manuscript entry names Cesena as its observation context.
claims.confidence_basis: The university chronology supplies the place name and folio locator; no point geometry is asserted.

claims.statement: The dated 6 September 1502 manuscript entry names Cesenatico as its port observation context.
claims.confidence_basis: The university chronology supplies the place name and folio locator; no point or port geometry is asserted.

claims.statement: Getty TGN record 7004864 identifies Imola for the selected place candidate.
claims.confidence_basis: The controlled-vocabulary record is attributable under ODC-By 1.0; historical geometry is not inferred from it.

claims.statement: The Process groups selected dated engineering observations as an analytical corpus and does not assert a continuous mechanism, cause or itinerary.
claims.confidence_basis: The grouping is a declared curation interpretation over the dated source records, not a historical assertion of continuity.

claims.statement: The Trajectory contains four source-bound presence contexts separated by three explicit gaps with unknown routes.
claims.confidence_basis: Dated Rimini, Cesena and Cesenatico entries plus the datable Imola context support anchors only; route evidence is absent.

claims.statement: The patent's ducal title supports a Duchy of Romagna political context but does not specify a territorial boundary.
claims.confidence_basis: The university-press patent transcription supports the title-based context; it supplies no polygon or boundary method.

claims.statement: A conservative alternative represents only the four documented named-place anchors and makes no claim about territory between them.
claims.confidence_basis: This alternative is a fail-closed analytical response to missing boundary evidence and unresolved derived-geometry rights.

claims.statement: Atçıl records that in 1502 an Ottoman authority forcibly displaced a large Turkmen group suspected of supporting Shah Isma'il to the Morea.
claims.confidence_basis: The Cambridge University Press article supplies a year-precision statement at printed p. 298 with note 13; review is pending.

uncertainties.description: Stable university-press locators bind the dated Rimini, Cesena and Cesenatico entries to folios 78r, 46v and 66v, but no rights-cleared facsimile is frozen. The separate Cesena wall-survey folios 9r–10r association relies only on the institutional itinerary in the frozen source set.
uncertainties.effect: The dated bibliographic locators remain reviewable. The separate Cesena wall-survey folio Claim is rejected from the Gate C supported Claim set and may return only after a critical-edition locator or rights-compliant facsimile is reviewed.
uncertainties.basis: The uncertainty is attached to the five atomic folio and dated-presence Claims that expose the locator boundary.

uncertainties.description: A university-press critical transcription is pinned, but the frozen source graph contains no original-document repository record, archival call number or rights-cleared surrogate.
uncertainties.effect: The date and commissioned title can undergo textual review, while original-object provenance, physical inspection and media reuse remain unresolved.
uncertainties.basis: The source registry has a transcription locator but no registered archival custody or surrogate source.

uncertainties.description: Current candidate locators point to live institutional pages whose wording may change.
uncertainties.effect: No Claim may become reviewed until a rights-compliant immutable artifact or stable bibliographic locator is frozen.
uncertainties.basis: Gate C preserves URLs and bibliographic locators but does not archive copyrighted source content.

uncertainties.description: The selected RCT context supports an autumn 1502 framing rather than an exact day.
uncertainties.effect: The Imola map-work Event must remain an approximate range and cannot be rendered as an exact instant.
uncertainties.basis: The Imola map-work Claim is bound to a catalogue range rather than an exact-date locator.

uncertainties.description: The selected slice does not establish the exact end of Leonardo's commissioned-service State.
uncertainties.effect: The State cannot silently use 31 December 1502 as a historical end date; that date is only the analytical slice boundary.
uncertainties.basis: No frozen EvidenceLink supplies an end date for the commissioned-service State.

uncertainties.description: No reviewed source-backed geometry defines the changing Duchy of Romagna boundary for the selected interval.
uncertainties.effect: Region geometry remains null and modern Emilia-Romagna cannot be substituted.
uncertainties.basis: The registered sources do not supply both a boundary method and affirmative derived-geometry rights.

uncertainties.description: One Safavid State and one year-precision Ottoman displacement Event are the only global simultaneity anchors in this sparse review slice.
uncertainties.effect: The package cannot imply representative world coverage or any relation to Leonardo.
uncertainties.basis: The gate intentionally selects only the smallest global pair needed to test simultaneous State and Event semantics.

uncertainties.description: The Process is a curator-defined grouping over selected observations, not evidence of a continuous historical mechanism or complete work programme.
uncertainties.effect: Renderers and projections must preserve the analytical label and cannot infer causality, continuity or completeness.
uncertainties.basis: The selection rule groups independently dated observations only to exercise Process semantics.

uncertainties.description: The frozen sources establish selected presence contexts but provide no reviewed route evidence between them.
uncertainties.effect: All three inter-place segments remain unknown_route with null geometry and cannot be projected as lines.
uncertainties.basis: No EvidenceLink in the package claims a path, corridor or travel mechanism between the four anchors.

uncertainties.description: The scholarly locator dates the forced displacement only to 1502 and does not supply a month or day.
uncertainties.effect: The Event has possible rather than certain overlap with the 8 August–31 December analytical interval and cannot render as an exact instant.
uncertainties.basis: The global Event Claim and its Cambridge locator expose year precision explicitly.
